entities.summary: Juan de Borja Lanzol de Romaní the Younger (1470–1500) was a Spanish Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a pivotal role in the Catholic Church's efforts to reform and centralize its institutions during the late 15th century. Born in Spain, Lanzol de Romaní rose through the ranks of the clergy, becoming a cardinal in 1500 and serving as a key advisor to Pope Alexander VI. His influence extended beyond the Vatican, as he worked to promote the interests of the Spanish monarchy and the Catholic Church in the kingdoms of Aragon and Castile. Lanzol de Romaní's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Catholic Church in Spanish politics and society, as well as the ongoing efforts to reform and centralize its institutions. The Spanish Inquisition, which was established during his lifetime, remains a significant example of the Church's role in shaping Spanish history. Through his work, Lanzol de Romaní contributed to the consolidation of power by the Catholic Church in the Iberian Peninsula and the emergence of the modern Spanish state.

entities.summary: Juan de Borja Lanzol de Romaní the Younger (1470–1500) was a Spanish Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal. He played a significant role in the Spanish Inquisition, serving as the Bishop of Toulouse and the Archbishop of Valencia. During his tenure, he implemented reforms aimed at reducing corruption and increasing the power of the Inquisition. His efforts led to the establishment of the Spanish Inquisition's permanent headquarters in Valencia. This led to a significant increase in the number of trials and executions, with some estimates suggesting that over 150,000 people were burned at the stake during the 16th century. Despite his efforts to reduce corruption, Lanzol de Romaní was criticized for his handling of cases involving Jews and Muslims. The Catholic Church eventually stripped him of his cardinalate due to his perceived conflicts of interest. Lanzol de Romaní died on January 26, 1500, while under house arrest for his perceived heresy. The legacy of Lanzol de Romaní continues to be felt in the history of the Spanish Inquisition, with many historians viewing him as a symbol of the Church's increasing authoritarianism during the 16th century.
